newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank rates held steady, assets statement due.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank rates held steady, assets statement due.

text.p: The German central bank left the country's key interest rates unchanged Wednesday after a regular meeting of its policy-setting council.
The Bundesbank left the discount rate at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also kept at 3 percent.
The central bank also announced that it would make a further statement later in the day on plans by the Bonn government to revalue the central bank's assets.

Few economists had expected a change in rates at the meeting, with discussions expected to focus on Bonn's plans to revalue the central bank's assets in a bid to shore up finances and meet entry criteria for the new European currency.

"A statement from the central bank council on the concept presented by the Finance Ministry with regard to the accounting systems of the German Bundesbank is likely to be released in the course of the later afternoon," the central bank said.
Government sources said Tuesday the central bank was expected to approve the revaluation of its gold reserves.
The Bundesbank has about 95 million ounces of gold valued in its books at well below current market levels.
